title: Cross-language SDK compatibility layer: unified streaming + tool-calls + structured-output examples
creator: Sofia Ramirez
description: Design and implement a compatibility shim in the TypeScript, Python, and Go SDKs that provides a consistent developer experience for streaming responses, function/tool calling, and structured outputs. The shim should: (1) accept legacy streaming token deltas and new structured delta events, (2) provide a ToolCallHandler abstraction that normalizes function/tool invocation lifecycles across languages, and (3) expose typed structured-output parsing helpers and examples so downstream apps can validate and migrate incrementally.
acceptance_criteria: TS/py/go SDKs expose a 'compat' module that normalizes streaming event shapes (legacy token deltas and new delta-event objects)
A ToolCallHandler interface exists in each SDK with lifecycle hooks: onInvoke, onResult, onError, and metrics emission
Structured output helper can validate JSON Schema and proto-like typed responses with minimal allocations and clear error messages
End-to-end example apps (chat + tool) in TS/Python/Go included in repo examples/compat-examples and linked in the ticket
Telemetry events for fallback behavior (how often legacy shape received) are emitted to the console and metrics sink for canary monitoring
Canary rollout plan defined: 10% of new hosted API traffic for 2 days, monitor regressions (latency, error rate, schema failures)
technical_notes: Compatibility design: stream frames will be normalized into an internal 'DeltaEvent' with fields {type, content, tool_call?: {...}, schema_tag?: string}. Keep this model internal to avoid coupling with runtime payloads.

Memory/CPU: Python streaming parser uses incremental JSON parsing (ijson) to avoid buffering entire responses for large streams; TypeScript uses transform streams; Go uses bufio.Reader with small buffers to support backpressure.
Tool calling: ToolCallHandler must support sync and async tool implementations. For TS/Go we provide examples showing promise/goroutine patterns; Python example uses asyncio and sync adapters.
Structured outputs: provide schema registry helpers that can fetch lightweight JSON Schema from a manifest and validate deltas as they arrive to fail-fast on incompatible outputs.

Compatibility heuristics: detect legacy format by presence of 'token' or 'delta' top-level keys; new structured events include 'event_type' or 'schema_tag'. Shim should prefer structured events when present, else convert legacy token stream to DeltaEvent with type 'token' for parity.
Metrics: add events: sdk.compat.fallback_count, sdk.compat.schema_validation_failures, sdk.compat.stream_lag_ms. These are counters/gauges emitted via existing telemetry adapter.

Security: ensure no remote code execution vectors in tool handler bindings. All tool-call payloads must be validated and sanitized before calling out to user-provided code. Security review required for new public interfaces (flagged below).
progress_updates: 2026-03-10 - Kickoff: scoped API surface. Drafted DeltaEvent shape and cross-language mapping (TS/Py/Go). Agreed to keep internal normalization and provide thin language-specific helpers.
2026-03-11 - TypeScript prototype: created streams/compat.ts that maps both legacy token deltas and new event objects into DeltaEvent. Initial unit tests added.
2026-03-12 - Python prototype: implemented incremental parser using ijson and created ToolCallHandler base class with asyncio-friendly hooks. Ran basic validation against stored sample streams.
2026-03-13 - Go prototype: implemented Reader-based parser and ToolCallHandler interface. Validated against synthetic streams. Began writing end-to-end example for chat-with-search tool integration.
2026-03-13 - PRs opened: github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pulls/4822 (ts), /4823 (py), /4824 (go). Linking to this ticket for reviews.
review_feedback: PM (Aisha Gupta): please include migration notes and a 'how to opt-in/opt-out' section for existing customers. Also ensure SDK major bump is not required for opt-in path.
Design (Marcel Nguyen): examples need clearer UX for tool call errors in streamed contexts - recommend standard 'tool-error' envelope and suggested UI patterns for consoles.
Security (Priya Banerjee): require mandatory security_review_required before GA due to tool-call surface (external code invocation). Added checklist for input validation and syscall limits.
Infra (Ethan Li): telemetry naming looks good but routing to metrics pipeline needs standardization. Use 'sdk.compat.*' prefix as proposed and add tags: sdk_lang and release_stage.
notes_for_release_engineering: Provide a feature flag (SDK side and server side) to enable compat layer per-client so we can canary without forcing server change for all clients.
Docs: add migration guide in SDK docs under 'Compatibility and streaming' with TS/Py/Go snippets and a table of behavioral diffs.
CI: add integration tests that replay recorded legacy streams and new structured-event streams to assert parity.
Rollout: canary to 10% for 48 hours, then 50% for 24 hours before general availability. Monitor sdk.compat.schema_validation_failures and http 5xxs.
